## Scope and reproducibility

This separate report compares `final_data`, generated by `scripts/create_final_data.R`, with `final_data_codex`, generated by `scripts/codex_final_data_script.R`. Both are rebuilt from the repository's raw files in separate R environments. Their CSV-writing expressions are excluded in memory; neither source script is edited. The saved `data/processed/final_data.csv` is also checked against the original script's result.

Render from the repository root with `quarto render reports/compare_final_data_codex.qmd`. R, Quarto, and the packages checked below must be installed. Inputs use relative repository paths; no existing workspace objects are required. Both complete source scripts are displayed in the appendix without executing their export steps.

```{r}
#| label: setup
required <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "janitor", "here", "knitr",
              "rmarkdown", "tidyverse", "countrycode", "flextable", "sjPlot")
missing_packages <- required[!vapply(required, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages)) stop("Install required packages: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
# Quarto normally executes relative to this document; also allow repository-root execution.
root <- if (file.exists("scripts/create_final_data.R")) "." else ".."
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root, "reports", "compare_final_data_codex.qmd")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(root))
```

```{r}
here::i_am("reports/compare_final_data_codex.qmd")
original_path <- "data/processed/final_data.csv"
codex_path <- "scripts/codex_final_data_script.R"
original_script <- "scripts/create_final_data.R"
inputs <- unique(c(original_path, original_script, codex_path,
            list.files("data", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE),
            list.files("scripts", full.names = TRUE)))
input_hashes <- tools::md5sum(inputs)
saved_original <- read.csv(original_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
original_code <- readLines(original_script, warn = FALSE)
codex_code <- readLines(codex_path, warn = FALSE)
call_name <- function(expr) {
  if (is.call(expr) && is.symbol(expr[[1]])) as.character(expr[[1]]) else ""
}
replay_without_export <- function(code) {
  expressions <- parse(text = code)
  calls <- vapply(expressions, call_name, character(1))
  stopifnot(sum(calls == "write.csv") == 1L)
  keep <- !calls %in% c("write.csv", "file.exists")
  env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
  invisible(capture.output(for (expr in expressions[keep]) eval(expr, env)))
  env
}
replay_env <- replay_without_export(original_code)
codex_env <- replay_without_export(codex_code)
original <- replay_env$final_data
codex <- codex_env$final_data_codex
show_table <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, ...)
```

## Comparison of script logic

| Step | Original script | Codex script | Implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mortality reshaping | Selects the column range `X2000:X2019`; year is numeric | Cleans names, recognizes four-digit year columns, filters 2000–2019; year is integer | Same intended years; different storage types and selection methods |
| Merge base | Full join of four mortality tables | Unique union of mortality keys followed by left joins | Same country-year coverage with these inputs |
| Disasters | Creates numeric indicators and takes group maxima | Uses `any()` and integer indicators | Both allow drought and earthquake in the same year |
| Missing disaster matches | Replaces missing indicators with zero after merging | Completes indicators on panel keys before merging | Same no-record assumption |
| Conflict deaths | `sum(best, na.rm = TRUE)` | Replaces missing-ID/missing-death placeholders with zero; otherwise `sum(best)` | Can differ for identified conflicts with missing death counts |
| Conflict threshold and lag | Threshold per conflict; country-year maximum; year plus one | Threshold per conflict; country-year `any()`; year plus one | Both represent previous-year exposure |
| Missing conflict matches | Retains missing values | Assigns zero when no record matches | Requires an explicit coverage assumption |
| Validation | Prints diagnostics | Also asserts key uniqueness and valid indicators | Codex stops on specified structural problems |
| Export | Writes `final_data.csv` | Writes `final_data_codex.csv` | Both exports are skipped by this report |

## Dimensions, names, and types

```{r}
show_table(data.frame(dataset = c("Original script in memory", "Codex script in memory"),
                      rows = c(nrow(original), nrow(codex)),
                      columns = c(ncol(original), ncol(codex)),
                      countries = c(length(unique(original$iso)), length(unique(codex$iso))),
                      first_year = c(min(original$year), min(codex$year)),
                      last_year = c(max(original$year), max(codex$year))))
name_map <- c(matmor = "maternal_mortality", infmor = "infant_mortality",
              neomor = "neonatal_mortality", un5mor = "under5_mortality",
              armed_conflict_lag1 = "armed_conflict")
aligned_names <- names(original)
mapped <- aligned_names %in% names(name_map)
aligned_names[mapped] <- unname(name_map[aligned_names[mapped]])
stopifnot(setequal(aligned_names, names(codex)))
show_table(data.frame(original_name = names(original), codex_name = aligned_names,
  original_position = seq_along(original), codex_position = match(aligned_names, names(codex)),
  original_type = vapply(original, typeof, character(1)),
  codex_type = vapply(codex[aligned_names], typeof, character(1)), row.names = NULL))
```

The four mortality names differ only in abbreviation. Codex's `armed_conflict` already refers to the **previous calendar year**, just like the original `armed_conflict_lag1`; it must not be lagged again. Drought and earthquake have different column positions. Both script outputs are tibbles. The original uses double-precision numbers for year and its binary exposure indicators; Codex explicitly uses integers. These storage differences do not imply different values.

## Observation keys and missing values

```{r}
keys <- c("iso", "year")
key_audit <- function(x) data.frame(missing_key_rows = sum(!complete.cases(x[keys])),
                                  duplicate_key_rows = sum(duplicated(x[keys])))
show_table(rbind(original = key_audit(original), codex = key_audit(codex)))
# Alignment must not hide duplicate observations.
stopifnot(all(complete.cases(original[keys])), all(complete.cases(codex[keys])),
          !anyDuplicated(original[keys]), !anyDuplicated(codex[keys]))
a <- original
names(a) <- aligned_names
b <- as.data.frame(codex)
only_original <- dplyr::anti_join(a[keys], b[keys], by = keys)
only_codex <- dplyr::anti_join(b[keys], a[keys], by = keys)
show_table(data.frame(observation_set = c("Only original", "Only Codex"),
                     rows = c(nrow(only_original), nrow(only_codex))))
show_table(only_original)
show_table(only_codex)
show_table(data.frame(variable = names(a), original_missing = colSums(is.na(a)),
                     codex_missing = colSums(is.na(b[names(a)])), row.names = NULL))
```

Missing outcome and covariate values are retained in both datasets. They should not automatically be replaced with zero. The following table locates missing mortality observations by year, and identifies countries with missing infant mortality.

```{r}
show_table(a |> dplyr::group_by(year) |> dplyr::summarise(
  dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("mortality"), ~sum(is.na(.x))), .groups = "drop"))
show_table(unique(a[is.na(a$infant_mortality), "iso", drop = FALSE]))
```

## Summary statistics

Statistics exclude missing values; missingness is reported separately. All numeric variables, including binary indicators and year, are shown. Maternal mortality is per 100,000 live births; infant, neonatal, and under-five mortality are per 1,000.

```{r}
numeric_summary <- function(x, label) {
  vars <- names(x)[vapply(x, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
    z <- x[[v]][!is.na(x[[v]])]
    data.frame(dataset = label, variable = v, n = length(z),
      mean = if(length(z)) mean(z) else NA_real_,
      sd = if(length(z) > 1) sd(z) else NA_real_,
      min = if(length(z)) min(z) else NA_real_,
      median = if(length(z)) median(z) else NA_real_,
      max = if(length(z)) max(z) else NA_real_)
  }))
}
summary_table <- rbind(numeric_summary(a, "Original"), numeric_summary(b, "Codex"))
show_table(summary_table[order(summary_table$variable, summary_table$dataset), ], digits = 6)
```

## Cell differences and equivalence

Exact cell comparisons treat paired missing values as equal. Numeric equivalence additionally permits `abs(x-y) <= 1e-10 * max(1, abs(x), abs(y))` per cell; nonnumeric values must match exactly. No rounding or imputation is used. Comparisons use common country-year keys, with unmatched observations counted separately above.

```{r}
canonical <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)[order(x$iso, x$year), sort(names(x)), drop = FALSE]
  rownames(x) <- NULL
  x
}
aa <- canonical(dplyr::semi_join(a, b[keys], by = keys))
bb <- canonical(dplyr::semi_join(b, a[keys], by = keys))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(aa[keys], bb[keys], check.attributes = FALSE)))
tolerance <- 1e-10
cell_equal <- function(x, y, tolerant = FALSE) {
  same <- is.na(x) & is.na(y)
  observed <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  same[observed] <- x[observed] == y[observed]
  if (tolerant && is.numeric(x) && is.numeric(y)) {
    same[observed] <- same[observed] | abs(x[observed] - y[observed]) <=
      tolerance * pmax(1, abs(x[observed]), abs(y[observed]))
  }
  same
}
differences <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(aa), function(v) {
  data.frame(variable = v,
    exact_differences = sum(!cell_equal(aa[[v]], bb[[v]])),
    differences_beyond_tolerance = sum(!cell_equal(aa[[v]], bb[[v]], TRUE)))
}))
show_table(differences)
cell_details <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(aa), function(v) {
  i <- which(!cell_equal(aa[[v]], bb[[v]]))
  data.frame(iso = aa$iso[i], year = aa$year[i], variable = rep(v, length(i)),
             original = as.character(aa[[v]][i]), codex = as.character(bb[[v]][i]))
}))
show_table(cell_details)
same_keys <- nrow(only_original) == 0 && nrow(only_codex) == 0
comparison <- data.frame(test = c(
  "Identical script outputs (including classes and names)",
  "Identical after row/column ordering only (retain original names)",
  "Identical after name mapping, ordering, and base data-frame conversion",
  "Equivalent values after mapping and ordering (numeric tolerance)"),
  result = c(identical(original, codex),
             identical(canonical(original), canonical(codex)),
             identical(canonical(a), canonical(b)),
             same_keys && all(differences$differences_beyond_tolerance == 0)))
show_table(comparison)
```

There are `r sum(differences$exact_differences)` exact cell differences on matched keys and `r nrow(only_original) + nrow(only_codex)` unmatched country-year observations. Ordering alone does not make the objects identical because variable names differ. After the explicit name mapping, ordering, and removal of tibble-specific attributes, strict identity is **`r identical(canonical(a), canonical(b))`**. Integer versus double storage can prevent strict identity even when every value agrees. Thus, matching missing-value totals and summary statistics are supported by a full cell-by-cell comparison, not just aggregate agreement.

## Reproduction of the original script

The original script was replayed above with its export and file-existence check excluded. Compare that result with the saved CSV. This separates reproducibility of the saved file from equivalence of the two scripts.

```{r}
replayed <- as.data.frame(original)
replay_comparison <- all.equal(canonical(saved_original), canonical(replayed),
                               check.attributes = FALSE, tolerance = tolerance)
show_table(data.frame(test = c("Saved CSV versus original script: strict identity",
                              "Saved CSV versus original script: value equivalence"),
 result = c(identical(canonical(saved_original), canonical(replayed)), isTRUE(replay_comparison))))
show_table(data.frame(variable = names(saved_original),
                      saved_csv_type = vapply(saved_original, typeof, character(1)),
                      replay_type = vapply(replayed[names(saved_original)], typeof, character(1)),
                      row.names = NULL))
# Simulate CSV export/import entirely in memory, using the original write.csv defaults.
serialize_csv <- function(x) {
  output <- character()
  con <- textConnection("output", "w", local = TRUE)
  write.csv(x, con, row.names = FALSE)
  close(con)
  read.csv(text = paste(output, collapse = "\n"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
roundtrip_identical <- identical(canonical(saved_original), canonical(serialize_csv(replayed)))
show_table(data.frame(test = "Strict identity after in-memory CSV export/import", result = roundtrip_identical))
```

The original uses `as.numeric()` for year and numeric constants in binary indicators. CSV import may infer these whole-number columns as integers. Such type changes can prevent strict identity with an in-memory replay without changing analytical values. The simulated CSV round trip tests the actual saved-data representation without writing a file.

## Interpretation and recommended corrections

The present comparison finds no substantive discrepancy between the two datasets. Both use the union of mortality country-year keys as the merge base, retain missing outcomes, aggregate disasters to country-year indicators, apply the 25-death threshold separately within each conflict, and shift exposure forward one calendar year. The README's description of additional disaster-only rows does not apply to the current Codex script.

The following checks distinguish current defects from potential risks:

```{r}
conflict_raw <- read.csv("data/raw/conflict.csv")
show_table(data.frame(check = c("Rows with missing best",
                               "Rows with both conflict_id and best missing",
                               "Rows with conflict_id present but best missing"),
 value = c(sum(is.na(conflict_raw$best)),
           sum(is.na(conflict_raw$conflict_id) & is.na(conflict_raw$best)),
           sum(!is.na(conflict_raw$conflict_id) & is.na(conflict_raw$best)))))
show_table(data.frame(source = c("Mortality merge base", "Covariates", "Disaster aggregate", "Conflict aggregate"),
 duplicate_keys = vapply(list(replay_env$wbdata, replay_env$covariates,
                             replay_env$disaster, replay_env$conflict),
                        function(x) sum(duplicated(x[keys])), integer(1))))
```

- **Missing conflict deaths:** the original `sum(best, na.rm = TRUE)` converts an entirely missing group to zero and can undercount a partially observed group. Here, all missing death counts have missing conflict IDs; there are no identified conflicts with missing death counts. Codex explicitly treats those rows as no-record placeholders, so the two implementations agree on these files. If identified conflicts have missing deaths in future inputs, preserve unknown totals rather than silently setting them to zero. Confirm the placeholder interpretation against source documentation before generalizing it.
- **Absent conflict records:** the original leaves unmatched conflict joins as `NA`, while Codex sets absent records to zero. There are no resulting missing conflict indicators in this comparison. Choose and document the appropriate rule for future inputs: absence supports a zero only if source coverage justifies it. Both scripts likewise interpret absent disaster records as no recorded event, not proof that an event could not have occurred.
- **Join safeguards:** the current source tables produce unique keys, and no row multiplication is observed. Add missing-key and duplicate-key assertions before each join to detect future input problems. The Codex script already has these checks.
- **Year selection:** `X2000:X2019` selects a contiguous range by position. This works for the current files but is vulnerable to reordered or inserted columns. Use explicit year names, for example `all_of(paste0("X", 2000:2019))`, and validate that all requested years exist. Codex instead recognizes year names with a regular expression and filters the year values.
- **Naming and documentation:** retain the original's explicit `armed_conflict_lag1` name or document Codex's lag clearly. Update the README's historical merge-base description if it is intended to describe the current script. The comment spelling “Draught” is cosmetic: the executed original filter correctly uses `"Drought"`.
- **Missing outcomes and dependencies:** missing maternal mortality in 2018–2019 is retained from the source; do not fill it with zeros. Investigate missingness before defining an analysis sample. Remove unused presentation packages from the original cleaning script when revising it, and record package versions for future reproducibility.

**Conclusion:** the original saved dataset is `r if (isTRUE(replay_comparison)) "reproducible in values from the current original script and raw files" else "not reproduced in values by the current original script"`. Its CSV representation is `r if (roundtrip_identical) "also reproduced exactly after an in-memory CSV round trip" else "not reproduced exactly after an in-memory CSV round trip"`. The independent Codex dataset is equivalent after documented variable renaming and ordering. This establishes computational reproduction for the local inputs, not external validation of source coverage, study eligibility, or the original paper's analytical sample.
